intent: Keep the race 4 geometry unchanged: five 16 mm sensors at x = -0.03 to +0.03 (15 mm pitch) with y = 0.06, on a 12 cm track with 3 cm wheels, 12 cm body and 0.8 kg mass. This isolates controller tuning for the Integrator. I expect oval finishes to hold near 18 to 20 of 20, s-bend finishes to stay around 13 of 20 or improve, and slalom to remain the main gap. I expect that gain or base_speed changes are needed to bring slalom line loss below 1 per run. I am considering a 7-sensor layout at ±0.03 m (about 10 mm pitch) for a later iteration, as coverage exploration only, and I am not committing to it now.
learning: Race 4 showed that moving the lead to y = 0.06 at ±0.03 m with 16 mm footprints gave the best oval result (20 of 20) and a real s-bend gain (13 of 20), but slalom still loses the line at 1.1 events with max_error at the limit. Geometry changes so far have all been single-variable tests, and widening or narrowing the spread has not fixed slalom. Next race: if slalom line loss falls below 1 with the controller tuned, geometry is no longer the limiter. If slalom line loss stays at 1 or more with max_error at 0.06 after controller changes, the 7-sensor coverage test becomes the next geometry candidate. Oval steering_oscillation (0.30) remains above 0.2, so the lead may need to move further forward (y about 0.065 to 0.07) in a later race, provided oval finishes hold.
rationale: Race 4 (entityR2A, score 578.99) is the best result so far. It kept the race 2 geometry (±0.03 m spread, 16 mm footprints, wheels, body and mass unchanged) and moved the sensor lead from y = 0.05 to y = 0.06. Oval now finishes 20 of 20 (mean progress 0.997, max_error 0.030, line loss 0.5), up from 15 of 20 in race 2. Oval steering_oscillation fell only slightly, from 0.311 to 0.302, and is still above the 0.2 threshold. Still, the Integrator's rule was that the lead stays at y = 0.06 if oscillation falls and oval finishes hold or improve, and both held. I am therefore keeping y = 0.06. S-bend improved to 13 of 20 finishes, with line loss at 0.55, but slalom still finishes 0 of 20 with 1.1 line-loss events per run and max_error at the 0.06 m off-track limit. This meets the Integrator's condition for holding geometry and tuning gains (line loss at 1 or more with max_error at the limit). Earlier spread changes already showed that widening to ±0.04 m hurt oval and did not fix slalom, and the off-track limit is fixed at 0.06 m for any allowed body_width, so body changes give no benefit here. The 7-sensor option the Integrator flagged as exploration has no race evidence. Testing it now would change coverage and force new weights while the controller is still being tuned, so I am deferring it.
